basics.name: Konrad Odell
basics.label: Healthcare Data Platforms & Agentic AI Systems
basics.summary:
I've been shipping software for twenty years. Since 2022 I've been on the architecture team at Moxe Health, a HIPAA-regulated clinical data exchange. The work is data platform and integration: Databricks lakehouse and Unity Catalog governance, FHIR pipelines, and for the last two years, evaluating LLM and agent approaches against real clinical and billing workloads: proofs of concept that had to prove their value before anyone built on them, and a clinical document generation pipeline.

On my own time I built and run ElectricityFinder, a paid subscription product for people shopping Texas retail electricity plans. It runs an LLM extraction pipeline in production behind an evaluation gate, plus the compliance work a regulated market requires. I also maintain the tooling I build with: MCP servers, a library of agent skills, and evaluation harnesses that decide what is allowed to ship.

The way I build with coding agents is a worker and verifier loop: one agent does the work, a separate one with fresh context has to prove it runs and does the thing before I accept it, and the ones that can't be verified don't ship. Most of my tooling exists to make that loop cheap, because a system that fails quietly costs more than one that breaks loudly.
